timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only stream in the ledger; no semantic events projected from this source.
Serial trajectory: probes binary behavior, writes core, writes and rewrites engine, writes offset, then times out.

parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Rust, no external crates, byte-identical output, std::env::args parsing, Cargo/rustc build, and root test3.rs, then expanded the task into a broad Clipper2 library contract.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned initial scaffold/core and delegated hidden tests plus four engine implementations, followed by planned judging, offset, integration, verification, and fixes.
parallel.implementation: Created Cargo.toml, clipper2/mod.rs, and clipper2/core.rs, built local harnesses and geometry probes, but did not install engine.rs, offset.rs, or test3.rs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration was assigned in the workflow but never reached because the workflow was killed during the hidden-test/engine fan-out; artifact validation listed only three files and no root entry.
parallel.verification: Ran C++ output probes and a Rust derivation of square-offset geometry, but no integrated Rust build or differential acceptance completed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Timed out with a killed workflow, no workflow result, missing /output/test3.rs, no executable, and 0/40 official tests passed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same prompt and confirmed the C++ binary output was always 1 for sampled arguments with exact two-byte stdout.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all work in the main actor with no subagents or delegated ownership.
serial.implementation: Created /output/src, wrote core.rs, wrote and rewrote engine.rs, and wrote offset.rs in the serial trajectory.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Did not create Cargo.toml or the required package-root test3.rs before timeout; artifact validation listed only src files.
serial.verification: Verified reference output behavior, but no Rust executable build or final differential test was completed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Timed out with no required root entry file or executable and 0/40 official tests passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent recognized the prompt requirements, probed the binary, and also expanded the task into a general Clipper2 engine and offset contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control recognized the same prompt requirements and confirmed the reference binary always printed 1 for sampled argument sets.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both knew the required entry file and output behavior, but parallel converted the simple deliverable into a much broader orchestrated library plan.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created task records and a workflow with hidden-test, engine, offset, judge, integration, verify, and fix ownership split across subagents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents and no delegation; the same actor wrote each implementation file directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel ownership was broad and staged across child workers, while serial ownership stayed local and sequential.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave children a detailed shared contract, API signatures, hard rules, and per-directory ownership constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried context in a single trajectory and did not need cross-agent handoff or interface reconciliation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel interface context was extensive and explicit; the failure was not missing contract information but the cost and stalls of executing the plan.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote Cargo.toml, clipper2/mod.rs, and a core.rs scaffold, then spent time deriving geometry and waiting on workflow children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed the binary and wrote src/core.rs, src/engine.rs, rewrote engine.rs, and wrote src/offset.rs before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial implemented more local modules, while parallel stopped with only the scaffold/core files and no engine.rs, offset.rs, or test3.rs artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow had no result, was killed, and child attempts remained stalled or errored before judging and integration could return anything to the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its only lifecycle issue was ordinary timeout before final packaging.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a child-result lifecycle that never completed, while serial had no subagent joins to perform.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel planned an integration child to write test3.rs and build, but that phase was downstream of unfinished judging and never ran.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote source files under src but never created the package-root entry file required by the prompt.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both missed final assembly, but parallel missed it because integration was gated behind stalled fan-out, while serial simply ran out after local module writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified pieces of its planned contract and derived geometry, but no integrated Rust binary was built or accepted; official evaluation passed 0/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified the C++ reference output by probing and xxd, but no final Rust build or evaluator-aligned acceptance occurred; official evaluation passed 0/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel invested in planned public/hidden/adversarial batteries that never completed, while serial did only direct reference-output probes before implementation timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after 2399 seconds, 36 subagents, 2.53M total tokens, and 1.24M workflow-child tokens.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out after about 2399 seconds, but with zero subagents, 347K total tokens, and only nine tool calls.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run spent far more budget on workflow children and retries, whereas serial spent its budget on local file generation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The completed official status for both modes reports solution_passed=false and 0 of 40 testcases passed, so the outcome relation is both_fail rather than discordant. The shared official failure is concrete artifact incompleteness: the required package-root test3.rs was absent in both artifacts. The task-solving difference is that parallel lost most of its time to a broad workflow fan-out and repeated stalled children, delivering only scaffold/core files, while serial made more direct implementation progress into core, engine, and offset modules but still failed to assemble the required entry file and executable.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out and stall retries consumed the parallel budget before integration and entry-file assembly.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided delegation and produced more module implementation, but still timed out before package-root assembly.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs overimplemented a broad Clipper2 library surface despite the visible sample only requiring the result length 1.
Serial placed files under src while the prompt required a package-root test3.rs, and parallel never reached entry-file creation at all.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Both failed officially; the retained parallel pattern explains a material completeness disadvantage but not a pass/fail differential.

candidates.reason: The parent wrote core.rs and assigned engine and offset implementation children, so implementation ownership existed even though work did not finish.
The workflow explicitly defined judge and integration phases, so integration was owned but never reached after the fan-out stall.
The integration child was explicitly assigned to write /output/test3.rs and build the deliverable, so assembly was owned but gated behind unfinished earlier stages.
The workflow script defined an end-to-end pipeline from hidden tests through fix, so the issue was budget exhaustion in execution rather than no pipeline owner.
No single mandatory serial preflight blocked productive work; hidden-test and engine children were launched concurrently.
The parent did some probing and specification work, but implementation fan-out started rather than waiting for a completed investigation phase.
The critical-path failure is better captured by collective workflow fan-out and repeated retry exhaustion, not by auxiliary work starving one narrow implementation path.

The parallel parent launched hidden-test and engine fan-out, then the workflow retried stalled children across six branches until it was killed. The run spent 1.24M workflow-child tokens and ended with only scaffold/core files, no entry file, no engine winner, no offset module, and no integrated build.
candidates.realized_consequence: Six live workflow branches and repeated stall retries consumed the finite run budget before any engine winner, offset implementation, integration child, root test3.rs, or executable was delivered.
candidates.near_match_reason: The repeated attempts resemble retry without checkpointing, but the earlier stalled attempts did not produce reusable implementation checkpoints or confirmed findings; the direct observed harm is collective fan-out and retry budget exhaustion.

candidates.reason: The child briefs were broad, but no single child was uniquely oversized relative to siblings; the realized episode was the aggregate fan-out/retry budget drain.
The child prompts included the shared contract, environment limits, exact API signatures, harnesses, and delivery boundaries for their assigned component work.
The workflow supplied shared module/API contracts and install destinations; no incompatible returned components reached integration.
There is no evidence that a known finding or constraint was lost during transfer between actors.
No completed child handoff containing usable information reached the parent and was left unconsumed because of volume.
No receiver acted on a handoff describing superseded workspace or requirement state.
No incompatible child reports or contracts arrived and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parent did not present the whole task as complete; final.txt was empty and the trajectory only promised to report back when fan-out landed.
Retry attempts restarted after stalls and repeated setup reads, but no prior attempt had produced a reusable checkpoint or confirmed finding; this is folded into the retained fan-out budget episode.

candidates.reason: Children were stalled and retried within the same workflow budget chain; treating termination separately would duplicate the retained fan-out exhaustion episode.
No complete engine/offset/test3 candidate or mutually compatible component set was ready for promotion before closure.
No child implementation was merged after verification; judging, integration, and verification were not reached.
No delegated implementation completed or became retrievable for the parent to join into the final implementation.
The workflow never reached the verifier phase, so no verifier child produced a trapped finding.
The stalled-child failures belong to the same fan-out/retry budget chain, and the parent had no separate post-failure takeover decision before timeout.
No completed child result was available to the parent and then ignored.
The parent launched the workflow and later timed out, but the material event is the workflow fan-out and stall retries rather than available progress being ignored during waiting.
No two completed child implementations claimed overlapping final behavior or required reconciliation.
No live same-file edit collision was observed.
No actor replaced a non-entry source file produced or owned by another actor.
No required executable or entry-point source existed to be overwritten.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another actor's final-tree work.
The workflow used shared directories, but no unstable state or provenance problem from shared writes materialized before the stalls.
No generated artifact, cache, fixture, temporary path, or tool output from one actor was consumed by another as stable reference input.

deduplicated_same_label_episodes: Repeated stall/retry cycles across the same six initial workflow branches were treated as one pair-level Fan-out Budget Exhaustion occurrence.
suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Critical-Path Starvation, Oversized Child Task, Early Child Termination, Blind Timeout Wait, No Failure Takeover, and Checkpoint-Free Retry were considered but rejected as the same stalled workflow budget chain or weaker near matches.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the aggregate fan-out/retry budget episode had a distinct realized parallel consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No downstream timeout, missing join, failure takeover, late finalization, or retry label was added for the same child-stall chain.
